description.content:
# Rewatch API

Rewatch is a self-hosted downloader (FastAPI + yt-dlp) rebuilt from [ReClip](https://github.com/averygan/reclip). This collection documents **every HTTP route the server exposes** and ships with tests, so it doubles as a smoke-test suite.

> **Version documented:** `1.0.0` (`app/__init__.py`). The server deliberately disables `/docs`, `/redoc` and `/openapi.json` (they return `404`), so this collection is the API reference.

## Quick start

1. Import `Rewatch.postman_collection.json` and `Rewatch.postman_environment.json`, then select the **Rewatch (local)** environment.
2. Start Rewatch (`python start_server.py` or `docker compose up`) and check `baseUrl` (default `http://localhost:8000`).
3. Run **Workflows → Video download** first. It creates a job, polls it until finished, downloads the file and checks the headers.
4. Run the whole collection from the Runner with a **delay of 2100 ms** between requests (see *Rate limiting*), or raise `REWATCH_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE`.

## Base URL and routes

| Area | Prefix | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| JSON API | `/api/v1` | `config`, `info`, `playlist`, `jobs…` |
| Infrastructure | `/` | `/healthz`, `/` (web page), `/robots.txt`, `/sitemap.xml`, `/favicon.ico`, `/static/*` |

## Authentication

There are **no accounts and no API keys**. Access control is a per-job token:

* `POST /api/v1/jobs` returns `{ "job_id", "token" }`.
* The token is `HMAC-SHA256(REWATCH_SECRET_KEY, job_id)` as hex, cut to 32 characters. Send it as the query parameter **`?token=`** on every `/jobs/{id}…` call.
* A missing token, a wrong token and an unknown job id all return the *same* `404 {"detail":"Job not found"}`, so job ids cannot be probed.
* Tokens never expire on their own, but jobs do (see *Job lifetime*). With a random secret key (the default when `REWATCH_SECRET_KEY` is empty) tokens stop working after a restart; jobs are in memory and never survive a restart anyway.
* Anyone who can reach the server can create jobs. Put it behind Cloudflare Access or a trusted network if it is exposed.

## Typical flow

```
POST /api/v1/info        -> title, thumbnail, available heights        (optional)
POST /api/v1/playlist    -> expand a playlist / TikTok photo post      (optional)
POST /api/v1/jobs        -> 202 {job_id, token}
GET  /api/v1/jobs/{id}/events?token=   (SSE)  or  GET /api/v1/jobs/{id}?token=  (poll)
GET  /api/v1/jobs/{id}/file?token=     -> the MP4 / MP3 / image
DELETE /api/v1/jobs/{id}?token=        -> cancel (only while queued or running)
```

## Job lifecycle

| `status` | Meaning | `progress` |
|---|---|---|
| `queued` | Waiting for a free worker | `0` |
| `downloading` | yt-dlp (or the slideshow downloader) is fetching streams | `0 – 94` (slideshows: up to `70`; single photo: `30`) |
| `processing` | ffmpeg is merging / converting | `96` |
| `done` | File is ready to download | `100` |
| `error` | Failed, see `error` (max 300 characters) | unchanged |
| `cancelled` | Stopped by `DELETE` | unchanged |

`done`, `error` and `cancelled` are **terminal**. `speed` (for example `"3.2 MB/s"`) and `eta` (seconds) are only set while downloading.

### Job lifetime

Finished jobs and their files are deleted `REWATCH_FILE_TTL_SECONDS` (default **1800 s**) after they finish. After that every call for that job returns `404`. Jobs stuck without finishing are swept after `max(2 x download timeout, 1 h)`.

## Errors

Every error uses FastAPI's shape:

```json
{ "detail": "Human readable message" }
```

Request-body validation errors (`422`) return `detail` as an **array** of Pydantic error objects instead:

```json
{ "detail": [ { "type": "string_too_short", "loc": ["body", "url"], "msg": "String should have at least 1 character", "input": "", "ctx": { "min_length": 1 } } ] }
```

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| `202` | Job accepted |
| `204` | Cancel accepted (empty body) |
| `400` | Unsafe or malformed URL, extractor failure (private video, unsupported site…), bad `audio_bitrate` |
| `404` | Unknown job, wrong or missing token, file not ready or expired |
| `422` | Body fails schema validation (wrong type, length, range, `format` not `video`/`audio`) |
| `429` | Rate limit (`Retry-After` = seconds) or download queue full (`Retry-After: 30`) |
| `504` | `info` / `playlist` took longer than `REWATCH_INFO_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` |
| `500` | Unhandled server error |

## Rate limiting

A sliding 60-second window **per client IP**, default **30 requests/minute** (`REWATCH_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE`, `0` = off, the Docker compose file uses `120`).

* It applies to **`POST /info`, `POST /playlist` and `POST /jobs` only**, and they share one bucket.
* **Invalid requests count too**, including `400` and `422` responses, because the limiter runs before validation.
* Status, events, file, cancel, `/config` and `/healthz` are not limited.
* Behind a proxy or tunnel set `REWATCH_TRUST_PROXY_HEADERS=true` so the limiter reads `CF-Connecting-IP` / `X-Forwarded-For`; otherwise all tunnel visitors share one bucket.
* A full 25-link batch in the web page needs about 50 counted requests (25 info + 25 jobs), which is more than the Python default of 30.

## Server limits (environment variables)

| Variable | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `REWATCH_MAX_CONCURRENT_DOWNLOADS` | `5` in code (`2` in `.env.example` and compose) | Worker threads |
| `REWATCH_MAX_QUEUED_JOBS` | `50` | Queued + running jobs; beyond it `POST /jobs` returns `429` |
| `REWATCH_MAX_PLAYLIST_ITEMS` | `50` | Entries returned by `/playlist` (`truncated: true` when cut) |
| `REWATCH_MAX_URLS_PER_BATCH` | `25` | Advertised in `/config`; only the web page enforces it |
| `REWATCH_MAX_DURATION_SECONDS` | `14400` | Longer media fails the job (`0` = off) |
| `REWATCH_MAX_FILESIZE_MB` | `2048` | Larger files fail the job (`0` = off) |
| `REWATCH_INFO_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | `60` | `info` / `playlist` timeout, then `504` |
| `REWATCH_DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | `1800` | Job fails with "Download timed out" |
| `REWATCH_FILE_TTL_SECONDS` | `1800` | Job and file lifetime after finishing |
| `REWATCH_ALLOWED_HOSTS` | empty | Comma-separated allow-list (matches the host and its subdomains) |
| `REWATCH_ALLOW_PRIVATE_URLS` | `false` | Allow private, loopback and link-local targets |
| `REWATCH_SLIDESHOW_MAX_PHOTOS` | `40` | Most photos used from a TikTok photo post (not listed in `.env.example`) |

## URL validation (applies to `info`, `playlist`, `jobs`)

A URL is rejected with `400` when it is empty or longer than 2048 characters, contains whitespace or control characters, is not `http`/`https`, carries `user:pass@` credentials, is not on `REWATCH_ALLOWED_HOSTS` (when set), or - **only when `REWATCH_ALLOW_PRIVATE_URLS=false`** - is `localhost` / `*.local` / `*.internal` / `*.localhost`, cannot be resolved (`Could not resolve host`), or resolves to **any** non-public address. With `REWATCH_ALLOW_PRIVATE_URLS=true` neither the name check nor the DNS lookup happens at all. DNS is resolved once before yt-dlp fetches the page, so this is a guard, not a full SSRF defence (redirects and DNS rebinding are not covered).

## Security headers on every response

`X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` and a strict `Content-Security-Policy` (same-origin scripts, styles, fonts and connections; `img-src` also allows `https:` for remote thumbnails). The collection-level test checks all three on every request.

## Collection variables

| Variable | Default | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| `baseUrl` | `http://localhost:8000` | Server address, no trailing slash |
| `mediaUrl` | a short public YouTube video | URL used by the info, job and workflow requests |
| `playlistUrl` | placeholder | Set to a real playlist URL to run the playlist request |
| `tiktokPhotoUrl` | placeholder | Set to a real `tiktok.com/@user/photo/<id>` URL to run the slideshow folder |
| `allowPrivateUrls` | `false` | Set `true` only if the server runs with `REWATCH_ALLOW_PRIVATE_URLS=true`; it skips the "private address is rejected" tests |
| `rateLimitEnabled` | `true` | Set `false` if the server runs with the limiter off; it skips the 429 test |
| `jobId`, `token`, `filename` | set by scripts | The job being followed |

Requests that need an external site (YouTube, playlists, TikTok) fail if the server has no internet access, the site blocks the server, or `REWATCH_ALLOWED_HOSTS` excludes it.
Health, configuration and the routes that serve the web page. None of these are rate limited.

They count towards the rate limit (see the collection description).

Reads a link's details without downloading it. For a playlist URL only the **first** entry is described.

### Request body

| Field | Type | Required | Rules |
|---|---|---|---|
| `url` | string | yes | 1 - 2048 characters, `http(s)`, public host. See *URL validation* in the collection description. |

### Response `200`

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `title` | string | Media title (may be empty) |
| `thumbnail` | string | `http(s)` image URL or `""`. Loaded directly from the source CDN by the web page. |
| `duration` | number or null | Seconds. `null` when unknown (for example a bare file URL) |
| `uploader` | string | Uploader or channel, `""` if unknown |
| `formats` | `{height, label, codec}[]` | One entry per resolution, highest first. With `REWATCH_PREFER_COMPATIBLE_CODECS=true` an H.264 stream wins ties. `codec` is `h264`, `vp9`, `av1`, `h265`, another prefix, or `""`. Can be empty. |
| `warning` | string | Non-fatal server problem, for example YouTube is missing Deno / `yt-dlp-ejs` so only a few qualities are listed |
| `photos` | integer | `> 0` only for a TikTok **photo post**; the number of photos (max `REWATCH_SLIDESHOW_MAX_PHOTOS`). `formats` is then `1080p` and `720p` (`h264`) |

### Notes

* TikTok app share links (`vm.tiktok.com/…`, `vt.tiktok.com/…`, `tiktok.com/t/…`) are followed (TikTok hosts only) and treated as a photo post when they resolve to `/@user/photo/<id>`.
* The `height` values in `formats` are what you pass as `height` when creating a job. They are not enforced: any other value just selects the closest stream at or below it.

### Errors

`400` unsafe URL or any yt-dlp failure (message is the last line of yt-dlp's error, ANSI codes stripped, max 300 characters, for example `Unsupported URL: …`, `Video unavailable`, `Private video`); `422` schema; `429`; `504` timeout.

The response is synthetic: `title` is `@user slideshow (N photos)`, `thumbnail` is the first photo, `duration` is `N x 3 s`, `photos` is `N`, and `formats` is always `1080p` and `720p` (`h264`). Results are cached in memory for 120 s because `info`, `playlist` and each photo job ask for the same list.

description.content:
Create, follow, download and cancel a download job.

Run the requests **in order**: *Create* stores `jobId` and `token` as collection variables, and the later requests use them. *Get job status* polls itself until the job is finished (Runner / `newman`), so the *Stream* and *Download* requests that follow always see a finished job.

Jobs are held **in memory** by a single process. Never run Rewatch with more than one worker.

Queues a download and returns immediately with `202`.

### Request body

| Field | Type | Default | Rules |
|---|---|---|---|
| `url` | string | required | 1 - 2048 chars, validated like `/info` |
| `format` | `"video"` or `"audio"` | `"video"` | Anything else is `422` |
| `height` | integer or null | `null` | 64 - 8640. Video only. Max resolution; `null` = best available. Ignored for audio and for single TikTok photos |
| `audio_bitrate` | integer or null | server default (`REWATCH_AUDIO_BITRATE_KBPS`, 192) | Audio only. **Must be 128, 192 or 320**, otherwise `400` (not `422`) |
| `title` | string | `""` | max 300 chars. Becomes the download filename |

### Output

* **video** is an H.264 + AAC `.mp4` when available (`REWATCH_PREFER_COMPATIBLE_CODECS=true`), merged by ffmpeg. The selector falls back to the best stream if no H.264 stream fits the height.
* **audio** is a `.mp3` re-encoded by ffmpeg at the chosen bitrate.
* **filename** is `title` (else the media title, else the job id) with `\ / : * ? " < > |` and control characters removed, trimmed of spaces and dots, cut to 100 characters, plus the extension. `"My: clip/1"` becomes `My clip1.mp4`.

### Response `202`

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `job_id` | 32-character hex id |
| `token` | Required as `?token=` for every follow-up call |

### Errors

* `400` unsafe URL, or `audio_bitrate must be one of [128, 192, 320]`
* `422` schema (bad `format`, `height` out of range, `title` too long, missing `url`)
* `429` rate limit (`Retry-After` seconds) **or** `Download queue is full — try again shortly` (`Retry-After: 30`) when `REWATCH_MAX_QUEUED_JOBS` queued + running jobs exist

Failures that happen *during* the download (live streams, duration or size limits, site errors) are reported on the job as `status: "error"`, not here.

description.content:
Returns the current state of a job. Safe to call repeatedly (the web page polls this every 1.2 s when the SSE stream drops).

In the Runner this request **re-runs itself every second until the job is terminal** (max 150 polls) using `setNextRequest`.

### Response `200` (`JobView`)

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | The job id |
| `status` | enum | `queued`, `downloading`, `processing`, `done`, `error`, `cancelled` |
| `progress` | number | 0 - 100 (see the lifecycle table) |
| `speed` | string or null | Human readable, for example `3.2 MB/s`; only while downloading |
| `eta` | integer or null | Seconds left; only while downloading |
| `filename` | string or null | The name the file will be downloaded as; set when `done` |
| `error` | string or null | Reason when `status` is `error` (max 300 chars) |

Server file paths are never exposed.

### Errors

`404` for a missing/wrong token, an unknown id, or a job older than its TTL. The response is identical in all three cases.

Common `error` strings: `Live streams are not supported`, `Media is longer than Nh limit`, `File is larger than the N MB limit`, `Download timed out`, `No file was produced (it may exceed the size limit)`, `Unexpected server error`, plus whatever yt-dlp reported (`Video unavailable`, `Private video`, `Sign in to confirm you're not a bot`…).

description.content:
Server-Sent Events stream of the same `JobView` object. The web page uses this first and falls back to polling.

* `Content-Type: text/event-stream`, `Cache-Control: no-store`, `X-Accel-Buffering: no`.
* The server checks the job every **0.5 s** and sends `data: {…JobView…}` **only when something changed**. The first frame is sent immediately.
* A `: ping` comment is sent after ~15 s of silence so Cloudflare's 100 s idle timeout does not cut the stream.
* The stream **closes by itself** after the frame whose status is terminal. Connecting to an already finished job returns that one frame and closes.
* If the job disappears mid-stream the server sends `event: gone` with `data: {}` and closes.
* Token or job errors are plain `404` responses *before* the stream starts (no SSE).

Postman shows an SSE body only once the connection closes, so run this on a finished job (as the Runner order does). For a live view use `curl -N` or the browser `EventSource`.

```text
data: {"id":"7a43…","status":"downloading","progress":41.5,"speed":"3.2 MB/s","eta":12,"filename":null,"error":null}

data: {"id":"7a43…","status":"done","progress":100.0,"speed":null,"eta":null,"filename":"My clip1.mp4","error":null}

```

description.content:
Returns the finished file as an attachment.

* `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename*=utf-8''<name>` (RFC 5987, so non-ASCII titles such as Khmer work).
* `Content-Type` is guessed from the extension: `video/mp4`, `audio/mpeg`, `image/jpeg`…
* `Accept-Ranges: bytes`, `ETag` and `Last-Modified` are set, so resumable downloads work.
* The file stays available until the job expires (`REWATCH_FILE_TTL_SECONDS`) and **can be downloaded repeatedly** in that time.

In Postman use **Send and Download** to save the binary.

`404 File not ready or expired` when the job is not `done` yet, the job expired, or the file vanished from disk. A bad token gives `404 Job not found`.

Asks the server to stop a **queued or running** job. Always returns `204` with an empty body when the token is valid and the job still exists.

Important behaviour:

* It only **raises a cancel flag**. A queued job is cancelled as soon as a worker picks it up; a downloading job notices within about 0.5 s, deletes its partial files and becomes `cancelled`. Poll *Get job status* to see it.
* For normal (yt-dlp) downloads the flag is only checked while bytes are downloading. Once `status` is `processing` (ffmpeg merge or MP3 conversion) the job runs to completion and ends as `done`. TikTok slideshow builds do check it during ffmpeg.
* On a **finished** job it is a no-op: the job and its file are **not** deleted and stay downloadable until the TTL expires.
* A cancelled job is removed after the normal TTL like any other finished job.
* Unknown id, wrong token or expired job: `404 Job not found`.

Extracts the audio track and encodes it to `.mp3` at 128, 192 or 320 kbps (`audio_bitrate`; omit it for the server default). `height` is ignored.

This request **overwrites `jobId` and `token`** so you can follow it with *Get job status* and *Download finished file*.

For a TikTok **photo post** the audio job saves the slideshow's music; if the post has no music the job ends with `This slideshow has no music to save`.

description.content:
TikTok **photo posts** (`/@user/photo/<id>`) can't be read by yt-dlp, so the server asks **gallery-dl** for the image and music URLs, downloads them from TikTok's CDN only (`tiktokcdn.com`, `tiktokcdn-us.com`, `tiktokv.com`, `tiktokv.us`, https only, redirects re-checked) and builds the result with **ffmpeg**.

| Job | Result |
|---|---|
| `format: "video"` | One portrait MP4 (H.264 + AAC, 30 fps): each photo shown **3 s**, music looped and cut with `-shortest`. `height` 1080 gives 1080x1920, 720 gives 720x1280 |
| `format: "audio"` | The post's music as MP3 |
| URL ending in `#image=N` | That one photo, original format, no ffmpeg. `format`, `height` and `audio_bitrate` are ignored |

Limits: 25 MB per image, 40 MB for the audio, `REWATCH_SLIDESHOW_MAX_PHOTOS` photos (default 40), the normal download timeout.

These requests need a real photo post URL in the `tiktokPhotoUrl` variable and are skipped while the placeholder is set.
